God says, "Children have I reared... but they have rebelled against me." What does God's grief show about his love?
God did not want empty offerings but to "learn to do good; seek justice." What does God want from your worship?
"Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow." What does this promise mean to you?
Nations will stream to the Lord's house and beat swords into ploughshares. What does this vision of peace stir in you?
"Come, let us walk in the light of the Lord." What does walking in God's light look like?
The Lord alone will be exalted in that day. What pride needs to be humbled in us?
God removes every support Jerusalem relied on. What do you lean on instead of God?
"Tell the righteous that it shall be well with them." How does this encourage you?
The Lord stands to judge those who crushed the poor. How does God see the poor?
In that day the branch of the Lord shall be beautiful and glorious. How does this point to Jesus?
God will create a cloud by day and fire by night as a shelter. How is God your shelter?
God planted a vineyard and asked, "What more was there to do?" What has God done for you?
Woe to those who add house to house and ignore the work of the Lord. Where might you be distracted from God?
"Woe to those who call evil good and good evil." Where do you see this today?
Isaiah saw the Lord high and lifted up, and the seraphim cried, "Holy, holy, holy." What does this vision show about God?
Isaiah cried, "Woe is me! For I am lost." How does seeing God's holiness show us ourselves?
The coal touched his lips: "Your guilt is taken away." How does God cleanse you?
"Whom shall I send?" Isaiah said, "Here I am! Send me." What might God be sending you to do?
"If you are not firm in faith, you will not be firm at all." Where do you need firm faith?
"The virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." How does this point to Jesus?
God told Isaiah not to fear what the people feared, but to fear the Lord. What do you fear more than God?
"I will wait for the Lord... and I will hope in him." What are you waiting for?
Should people consult the dead instead of their God? Where do people look for guidance today?
"The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light." Where do you need God's light?
"Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace." Which name of Jesus do you need today?
"Of the increase of his government and of peace there will be no end." What does Jesus' never-ending reign mean to you?
Woe to those who make unjust laws and rob the poor. How does God view injustice?
Assyria boasted, but God used it as a tool. What does this teach about pride and God's control?
A remnant will lean on the Lord in truth. What does leaning on God look like?
A shoot from the stump of Jesse will rule with righteousness. How does this describe Jesus?
The wolf will dwell with the lamb. What does this picture of peace show about God's future?
"The earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord as the waters cover the sea." How can you share that knowledge?
"Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and will not be afraid." What fear can you trust God with?
"With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation." What joy does salvation bring you?
"Make known his deeds among the peoples." What deed of God would you share?
The day of the Lord comes with judgement on pride. What does this teach about God's justice?
Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, would be overthrown. What does this say about the kingdoms of this world?
The Lord will have compassion on Jacob. What does God's compassion mean to you?
The proud one said, "I will ascend... I will make myself like the Most High." How does pride show itself?
"As I have planned, so shall it be." How does God's sure plan comfort you?
Isaiah weeps over Moab's destruction. What does it show that God's prophet grieves even for enemies?
Isaiah says, "My heart cries out for Moab." How can you have compassion even for those who oppose God's people?
A throne will be established in steadfast love, and on it will sit one who seeks justice. How does this point to Jesus?
Moab's pride brought its downfall. How does pride lead to ruin?
In that day people will look to their Maker, not to their altars. What do you look to?
"You have forgotten the God of your salvation." What causes us to forget God?
The Lord looks on quietly like clear heat in sunshine. What does God's quiet watching teach you?
Gifts will be brought to the Lord from a distant nation. What does this show about God's heart for the nations?
There will be an altar to the Lord in Egypt, and God will heal them. What does this show about God's mercy to all?
God says, "Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance." What does this show about God's plan?
Isaiah acted out a warning not to trust Egypt. What do people trust in instead of God?
People would be dismayed at what they had hoped in. What happens when we trust in the wrong things?
The watchman announces Babylon has fallen. What does it mean to watch for God's work?
"Watchman, what time of the night?" "Morning comes, and also the night." How do you wait through long nights?
They prepared their defences but did not look to God who made it. Where do you rely on your own plans?
God called for repentance, but they said, "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die." How do people avoid facing God?
God gives Eliakim the key of David. How does Revelation use this of Jesus?
The Lord planned to bring down the pride of Tyre. What does this show about wealth and pride?
Tyre's profits would one day be holy to the Lord. How can wealth be used for God?
The earth lies defiled under its inhabitants. What does this say about sin's effect on the world?
From the ends of the earth they sing, "Glory to the Righteous One." Where do you see people praising God worldwide?
The Lord of hosts will reign. How does God's reign give you hope?
"O Lord, you are my God; I will exalt you... for you have done wonderful things." What wonderful things has God done for you?
God will swallow up death forever and wipe away tears from all faces. What does this hope mean to you?
"Behold, this is our God; we have waited for him." What are you waiting for God to do?
"You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you." How can you fix your mind on God?
"My soul yearns for you in the night." When do you most long for God?
"Your dead shall live." How does this point to the resurrection?
God sings over his vineyard: "I, the Lord, am its keeper." How does God keep you?
God will gather his people one by one. What does it mean that God gathers each person?
The Lord will be a crown of glory to his people. What does that mean?
God lays in Zion a tested and precious cornerstone. How is Jesus that cornerstone?
The farmer's wisdom comes from God. How does God's wisdom show up in ordinary work?
"This people draw near with their mouth... while their hearts are far from me." Where might your worship be just words?
The deaf shall hear and the blind shall see. How did Jesus fulfil this?
"In returning and rest you shall be saved; in quietness and in trust shall be your strength." Where do you need quiet trust?
"The Lord waits to be gracious to you." What does this show about God?
"This is the way, walk in it." How does God guide you?
Woe to those who rely on horses but do not look to the Holy One. What are your "horses"?
Like birds hovering, the Lord will protect Jerusalem. How does this picture of protection comfort you?
A king will reign in righteousness, like a hiding place from the wind. How does Jesus fulfil this?
When the Spirit is poured out, the effect of righteousness will be peace. What does the Spirit bring to your life?
"O Lord, be gracious to us; we wait for you. Be our arm every morning." How can you pray this today?
"The fear of the Lord is Zion's treasure." What does it mean that fearing God is a treasure?
"Your eyes will behold the king in his beauty." What do you long to see of God?
"The Lord is our judge; the Lord is our lawgiver; the Lord is our king; he will save us." Which of these speaks to you?
All nations are called to listen to God's judgement. Why does God's justice matter?
"Seek and read from the book of the Lord." How can you seek God in Scripture?
"The desert shall rejoice and blossom like the crocus." Where do you long for God to make dry places bloom?
"Say to those who have an anxious heart, 'Be strong; fear not! Behold, your God will come.'" Who needs this message from you?
The blind see and the lame leap. How does Jesus fulfil this?
"The ransomed of the Lord shall return and come to Zion with singing." What joy awaits God's people?
The Assyrian asked, "On what do you rest this trust of yours?" How would you answer?
The people kept silent as Hezekiah commanded. When is silence wise?
Hezekiah went into the house of the Lord in distress. Where do you go when you are afraid?
Hezekiah spread the letter before the Lord and prayed. What can you spread before God?
God said, "I will defend this city to save it." How has God defended you?
God said, "I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears." What does this show about God?
"You have cast all my sins behind your back." What does this picture mean to you?
"The living, the living, he thanks you." How can you thank God for life?
Hezekiah showed the Babylonians all his treasures. How can pride show itself after blessing?
Hezekiah was content that peace would last in his days. How do our choices affect the next generation?
"Comfort, comfort my people, says your God." Where do you need God's comfort?
"The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God will stand forever." How does this steady you?
"He will tend his flock like a shepherd; he will gather the lambs in his arms." How has God carried you?
"They who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength." Where do you need new strength?
"Fear not, for I am with you; be not dismayed, for I am your God." What fear does this answer for you?
"I am the one who helps you." How has God helped you?
God promises water for the poor and needy. What thirst do you need God to satisfy?
God's servant will not break a bruised reed. How does Jesus treat the weak?
The servant is a light for the nations, opening blind eyes. How can you share his light?
"I will lead the blind in a way that they do not know." Where do you need God's leading?
"Fear not, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine." What does it mean to be called by name?
"When you pass through the waters, I will be with you." What waters are you passing through?
"Behold, I am doing a new thing." What new thing might God be doing in your life?
"I am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake." What does this mean to you?
God promises to pour his Spirit on your descendants. What do you pray for the next generation?
"Besides me there is no god... Is there a God besides me? There is no Rock." How does God's uniqueness comfort you?
Isaiah shows the foolishness of idols made from the same wood used for fire. What are modern idols?
"Return to me, for I have redeemed you." Where do you need to return to God?
"I am the Lord, and there is no other." How does this shape your trust?
Isaiah asks, "Does the clay say to him who forms it, 'What are you making?'" How do you respond to God's ways?
"Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth!" What does this show about God's invitation?
"Even to your old age I am he... I will carry and will save." How has God carried you through life?
"My counsel shall stand." How does God's sure plan give you peace?
"Our Redeemer, the Lord of hosts is his name, the Holy One of Israel." What does it mean that God is your Redeemer?
Babylon said, "I am, and there is no one besides me." How does self-sufficiency show up in us?
"I have refined you... in the furnace of affliction." How has God refined you?
"I am the Lord your God, who teaches you to profit, who leads you in the way you should go." Where do you need God's teaching?
"Oh that you had paid attention to my commandments! Then your peace would have been like a river." What peace comes from obedience?
The servant will be a light to the nations so God's salvation reaches the end of the earth. How does this point to Jesus?
"Can a woman forget her nursing child?... Yet I will not forget you." What does this show about God's love?
"I have engraved you on the palms of my hands." What does this picture mean to you?
"The Lord God has given me the tongue of those who are taught, that I may know how to sustain with a word him who is weary." Who could you sustain with a word?
The servant gave his back to those who strike. How does this point to Jesus' suffering?
"Let him who walks in darkness and has no light trust in the name of the Lord." What does trusting God in darkness look like?
"Look to the rock from which you were hewn." How does remembering God's past work help you?
"My salvation will be forever." How does God's lasting salvation steady you?
"Everlasting joy shall be upon their heads." What joy does God promise?
"I, I am he who comforts you; who are you that you are afraid of man?" What fear of others do you need to let go?
"How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news." How can you bring good news?
"All the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God." How does this encourage mission?
God's servant will be high and lifted up, yet his appearance was marred. How does this describe Jesus?
"He was despised and rejected by men; a man of sorrows." How does this describe Jesus?
"He was pierced for our transgressions... with his wounds we are healed." What does this mean to you?
"All we like sheep have gone astray... and the Lord has laid on him the iniquity of us all." How does this speak to you?
After his suffering, the servant will see and be satisfied. What does this show about the result of the cross?
God says, "Enlarge the place of your tent." Where might God be enlarging your life?
"With everlasting love I will have compassion on you." How have you known God's compassion?
"My steadfast love shall not depart from you." What does this unshakeable love mean to you?
"No weapon that is fashioned against you shall succeed." How does this encourage you?
"Come, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters... Why do you spend your money for that which is not bread?" What are you spending yourself on that doesn't satisfy?
"Seek the Lord while he may be found... he will abundantly pardon." What does God's abundant pardon mean to you?
"My thoughts are not your thoughts." How do you trust God when you don't understand?
God's word "shall not return to me empty." How have you seen God's word bear fruit?
"Keep justice, and do righteousness, for soon my salvation will come." What does doing righteousness look like for you?
"My house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples." How can your church welcome all peoples?
God dwells "with him who is of a contrite and lowly spirit, to revive the spirit of the lowly." What does this show about who God draws near to?
"I have seen his ways, but I will heal him." What does God's healing mean to you?
God says the fast he chooses is to loose the bonds of wickedness and share bread with the hungry. How could you live out this kind of fast?
"Your light shall break forth like the dawn." How does serving others bring light?
Calling the Sabbath a delight. How can rest be a delight for you?
"The Lord's hand is not shortened... but your iniquities have made a separation." What separates people from God?
God saw there was no one to intercede, so his own arm brought salvation. How does this point to Jesus?
"A Redeemer will come to Zion." How has Jesus come as your Redeemer?
"Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you." How can you shine?
"The Lord will be your everlasting light." What does this hope mean to you?
The Lord's anointed brings good news to the poor and binds up the brokenhearted. How did Jesus fulfil this?
God gives "a beautiful headdress instead of ashes, the oil of gladness instead of mourning." What exchange do you need?
"He has clothed me with the garments of salvation." How does God clothe you?
God gives his people a new name: "My Delight Is in Her." What does it mean that God delights in you?
God sets watchmen to pray and give him no rest. How can you pray persistently?
"I will recount the steadfast love of the Lord." What can you recount of God's love?
"In all their affliction he was afflicted... in his love and in his pity he redeemed them." How does God share in your suffering?
"You, O Lord, are our Father, our Redeemer from of old." What does God as Father mean to you?
"Oh that you would rend the heavens and come down." Where do you long for God to act?
"No eye has seen a God besides you, who acts for those who wait for him." How has God acted for you?
"We are the clay, and you are our potter." How do you let God shape you?
"I was ready to be sought by those who did not ask for me." What does this show about God's grace?
"I create new heavens and a new earth... no more shall be heard in it the sound of weeping." What do you look forward to most?
"Before they call I will answer." How has God answered before you asked?
"This is the one to whom I will look: he who is humble and contrite in spirit and trembles at my word." How do you respond to God's word?
"As one whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you." How has God comforted you?
All flesh shall come to worship before God. What does this vision show about God's plan?
